tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. # Method: a skill-text gate

This method is pre-registered for an Experiment whose instrument does not
exist yet. The instrument decides whether a change to a skill's text
(`skills/*/SKILL.md`) ships: the change ships only when a fresh agent
runner, started from a recorded point of a hyp tree, shows a failure in 3
or more of 5 trials with the skills as they are, and in 1 or fewer of 5
with the changed text.

## What one trial is

- One hyp sandbox per trial. The sandbox is made from this repository at a
  pinned commit, with the tree's store copied in at a store cut
  (`hyp sandbox create ... --store SRC --cut EVENT`). The store and the
  cut are given at run time; the instrument takes them as they are.
- An arm is the set of skill files the runner loads: `base` is the two hyp
  skills as the sandbox's commit has them; any other arm is a directory of
  `SKILL.md` files laid over them, one per skill it changes. The variant
  directories are part of the instrument. The runner's hyp is the same in
  every arm.
- Before the runner starts, the sandbox holds only hyp's code, the two
  skills (with the arm's variant over them) and the tree at the cut: no
  agent files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude` beyond the skills), no
  plans.
- The runner is a fresh `claude -p` session with the model `sonnet`, given
  a brief on stdin and project settings only. It is stopped after 50
  minutes. Its session transcript is kept with the trial's evidence, as is
  a summary of its run (exit, turns, cost).
- After the runner ends, the sandbox is removed and its changes kept, so
  the trial's evidence holds the transcript and every file the runner
  added or changed, its tree's events included.

## Scoring one trial

A score command reads one trial's evidence and prints `key<TAB>value`
lines:

- `arm`, `trial`;
- `skill_loaded`: 1 when the runner loaded a skill (a Skill tool call, or a
  Read of a `SKILL.md`);
- `failing_hyp`: the number of Bash calls that ended in error with `hyp` as
  the command whose exit status the call returns;
- one 0/1 fingerprint per row the gate is asked about:
  - `f_reading_pin`: an errored tool result holds hyp's refusal of an
    Experiment that declares `--decided-by reading` while it pins a recipe;
  - `f_body_limit`: an errored tool result holds hyp's refusal of a body
    over 600 runes.
- `end_state`: `recorded` when the runner's events record a Result,
  `registered` when they add an Experiment but no Result, else `none`.

## The gate

A verdict command reads the score of every trial, with the rows to judge
given as arguments, and needs exactly 5 trials per arm with distinct trial
numbers. For each row and arm, k is the number of trials whose fingerprint
is 1. A trial that never loaded a skill counts against its arm: for
`base` it is never a reproduction, for any other arm it always counts as a
failure.

- A row reproduces when `base` has k >= 3.
- A variant arm passes a row at k <= 1.
- It prints `verdict: repro=supports` when any row given reproduces, else
  `verdict: repro=contradicts`; and for each variant arm
  `verdict: ARM=supports` when it passes every reproducing row,
  `contradicts` when it fails one, and `inconclusive` when no row
  reproduces.

Both commands need known answers that cover every field and every verdict
branch, written by hand from the rules above.

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

# hyp-verification

This skill runs one Experiment (`E-` id) created by the hyp-prototype skill and
leaves evidence that a verifier can check without you. It does not decide what
the result means; that is the `hyp record` verdict.

## Find or write a recipe

- A recipe is a repeatable procedure, a bundle `recipes/<name>@<version>/`.
  hyp looks
  in `recipes/` beside `.tree/`, then in each parent directory up to the
  repository root, so list `recipes/` at each of those levels, read the one
  that fits, and cite it as `--recipe <name>@<version>`.
- When none fits and the procedure will be repeated, write one from
  [recipe-template.md](recipe-template.md) following
  [RECIPE-FORMAT.md](RECIPE-FORMAT.md), as `recipes/<name>@<version>/` in
  the repository-root library. To change a recipe, run
  `hyp recipe new <name>@<N+1> --from <name>@<N>` and edit the copy;
  never edit an existing version. Any byte change in a bundle is a new
  version, and a new version needs its known answers (RECIPE-FORMAT.md,
  Changing a recipe and Known answers). A verdict a measure decides
  needs a recipe that holds it (RECIPE-FORMAT.md, Verdict scripts);
  `--recipe none` with `--decided-by reading` is for a verdict decided
  by reading.
- `hyp add exp ... --recipe <name>@<version>` stores a hash of the recipe (the
  file, or every file of a bundle directory).
  A changed recipe is a new version. Old Results that followed the
  earlier text are then flagged questionable in `hyp status` and `hyp check`,
  which is the point: they were obtained with a different procedure.
  A bundle's commands are run by hyp: Launch and Doctor by
  `hyp sandbox create --recipe`, Drive by `hyp sandbox drive ID`, and
  Cleanup by `hyp sandbox remove`. After remove,
  `hyp recipe evidence --record DIR REF OUT_DIR` runs scripted Evidence,
  and `hyp recipe run --record DIR REF NAME ARGS` runs a Standalone
  command. When the sandbox ran them, Launch and Doctor are already done.
  Never run a bundle's script yourself (`docs/replay-spec.md` §9; the words
  are in `docs/glossary.md`, the decision in
  `docs/adr/0001-hyp-runs-every-recipe-command.md`).
- A bundle with an Evidence or Standalone command is an instrument and
  must have known answers. hyp runs them before every
  `hyp sandbox create`, `hyp recipe run` and `hyp recipe evidence`, and
  refuses the run when a case fails; that gate is the re-test of every
  version (`docs/adr/0002-known-answers-gate-every-recipe-run.md`).
  `hyp add exp --recipe <name>@<version>` refuses an instrument with no
  case, and any bundle whose `recipe.md` has no `format: 1` line.
- Before opening a pull request that touches `recipes/`, run
  `hyp recipe check` from anywhere in the repository. Exit 1 names the
  tree, the Result, the file and both hashes of a cited bundle that was
  edited in place: restore it and make the change as a new version.

## Launch

Start the subject under test: the app, a script, a database. Work from the
repository root and use seed or test data only, never real customer or
organization data. Note every process you start (command, PID, port) so you
can stop exactly those later.

## Doctor

Prove the subject is healthy before testing anything: it answers on its port,
the database is the test one, migrations are applied, the build is the
revision you meant. An experiment run against a broken subject says nothing
about the hypothesis; fix the subject or record the result as inconclusive.

## Drive

Perform the steps the Experiment's title and recipe describe, exactly. When
reality forces a deviation, write it down; a deviation that matters makes the
result inconclusive rather than supporting.

## Evidence

Evidence comes in two kinds. Evidence gathered by hand is what you save
while the sandbox still exists, before Cleanup, as below. Scripted Evidence
is a recipe's `## Evidence` command. Run it after remove with
`hyp recipe evidence --record .tree/evidence/<E-id>/<name> REF OUT_DIR`,
and again into a new directory to re-run it. hyp exits with the check's own
exit code. Cite its `command.json` and output, and never run its script
yourself.

A script whose output your verdict counts is a recipe command too
(RECIPE-FORMAT.md, Verdict scripts). Cite its `recipes/<name>@<version>/<script>`
pointer and its `command.json`, whose `known_answers` show the gate
passed. If `hyp record` prints `warn: uncontained`, fix what it names
before you select.

Store what you observed by hand under `.tree/evidence/<E-id>/`, with short file names:
command output, logs, timings, screenshots, the revision (`git rev-parse HEAD`).
Then record it with the hyp-prototype skill:
`hyp record --exp <E-id> --verdict <H-id>=supports|contradicts|inconclusive --observation "..." --evidence .tree/evidence/<E-id>/<file> --why "..."`.
Evidence must let someone who was not there judge the claim.

## Cleanup

Stop every process you started, by PID, and remove temporary data you created.
Never kill a process you did not start. Note anything you could not clean up in
an evidence file.

# skill-gate

A sandbox's Launch, Doctor, Drive and Cleanup for one trial of a fresh
Claude Code runner. It drives `claude -p` only; a runner for another
harness is another base. Create the sandbox with `--inputs FILE`, and
with `--store SRC --cut EVENT` when the runner starts from a tree at a
store cut; `--hyp BIN` pins the hyp the runner calls.

A Standalone check that scores one trial OUT_DIR, as `hyp sandbox remove`
left it with the runner's `state.env` and `transcript.jsonl` kept. It reads
the Claude Code transcript format.

A Standalone check that applies a reproduce-then-pass gate to the score
files of an Experiment's trials, one batched call after every trial ran.
Its thresholds are command-line arguments, so the Experiment's body
pre-registers the rule by quoting the command line.

## Launch

Run: ./launch.sh

Reads the inputs file, `KEY=VALUE` lines `arm`, `trial` and `model`, and
exits 2 when one is missing. It copies the inputs to this recipe's tmp as
`state.env`, deletes the paths in `STRIP` from `wt/`, copies the two hyp
skills into `wt/.claude/skills/`, and writes `brief.txt` followed by
`method.md` to this recipe's tmp as the runner's brief. Edit `STRIP`,
`brief.txt` and `method.md` for your method.

## Doctor

Run: ./doctor.sh

Passes when `claude`, `python3` and the pinned `hyp` run, the stripped
paths are gone, `.claude/` holds only `skills/` and the brief exists.

## Drive

Run: ./drive.py

Runs `claude -p --model MODEL --setting-sources project --permission-mode
dontAsk --allowedTools Bash Read Edit Write Glob Grep Skill` in `wt/` with
the brief on stdin, without `HYP_*` or `CLAUDE_CODE_*` variables and with
`HYP_ACTOR=runner-<arm>-<trial>`, and stops it after 50 minutes. It copies
the session transcript to this recipe's tmp as `transcript.jsonl` and
writes `drive.json` (arm, trial, model, exit, turns, cost_usd, denials).
It exits 1 when no transcript was written.

## Evidence

Kept by hand at remove: `--keep tmp/<name>/state.env --keep
tmp/<name>/drive.json --keep tmp/<name>/transcript.jsonl`, with `<name>`
this bundle's name. What the runner changed reaches OUT_DIR through
`changes/` and `changes.json`.

## Cleanup

Run: ./cleanup.sh

Nothing is left running: Drive waits for the runner to end.

## Standalone

Run score: ./score.py
External: none

- `score OUT_DIR` prints `key<TAB>value` lines: `arm`, `trial`,
  `skill_loaded`, `tool_calls`, `failing_hyp`, one `f_<name>` per entry
  of `FINGERPRINTS`, `stops` (failing_hyp plus every fingerprint) and
  `changed`. The script's docstring defines each field. It exits 2 when
  OUT_DIR lacks `state.env`, `transcript.jsonl` or `changes.json`.
  Edit `FINGERPRINTS` for your method, and give each a case that hits it.

`known-answers/` holds a clean trial (a skill load, an error that is not a
hyp call, a hyp call that succeeds), a trial with two failing hyp calls
and a refusal, a trial with no transcript and a usage failure. Every
expected output was written by hand from the docstring.

Run verdict: ./verdict.py
External: none

- `verdict --field F --base ARM --trials N --repro R --pass P SCORE...`
  reads one score file per trial (`arm`, `trial` and `F`). A trial fails
  when its `F` is not 0. It prints one line per arm and `verdict:
  repro=…`, then `verdict: ARM=…` for every other arm. The script's
  docstring states the rule. It exits 2 on a usage error, a missing
  field, no base arm, or an arm without exactly N distinct trials.

`known-answers/` holds a reproducing base with a passing arm, a
reproducing base with a failing arm, a base that does not reproduce, an arm with four trials, a missing
field and a missing base arm. Every expected output was written by hand
from the docstring.

from the runner's tmp, and changes.json written by remove. Prints
key<TAB>value lines:

  arm, trial      from state.env

  tool_calls      every tool call the runner made

                  bodies dropped)

  stops           failing_hyp plus every f_ value
  changed         paths remove lists as added or modified

A fingerprint is (name, where, pattern): where is "error" (the text of an
errored tool result), "bash" (a Bash command) or "path" (a changed path).
Edit FINGERPRINTS for your method; each one needs a known-answer case that
hits it. This script reads files only and calls no hyp. Exits 2 when OUT_DIR
lacks state.env, transcript.jsonl or changes.json, and 0 otherwise.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

FINGERPRINTS = [
    ("refused", "error", r"^refused: "),
]

LAST_HYP = re.compile(r"^(\w+=\S*\s+)*(\S*/)?hyp\s+[a-z-]")
HEREDOC = re.compile(r"<<-?\s*['\"]?(\w+)['\"]?[^\n]*\n.*?\n\s*\1\s*(?=\n|$)", re.S)


def last_command(cmd):
    """The command whose exit status a Bash call returns: heredoc bodies dropped, then
    the last part after a newline, ;, && or ||, and after its last |."""
    parts = [p.strip() for p in re.split(r"\n|;|&&|\|\|", HEREDOC.sub("", cmd)) if p.strip()]
    return parts[-1].split("|")[-1].strip() if parts else ""


def fail(msg):
    print("score: " + msg, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def blocks(lines, kind, role):
    for l in lines:
        content = (l.get("message") or {}).get("content")
        if l.get("type") == role and isinstance(content, list):
            for b in content:
                if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == kind:
                    yield b


def text_of(block):
    c = block.get("content")
    if isinstance(c, list):
        return "\n".join(x.get("text", "") for x in c if isinstance(x, dict))
    return c if isinstance(c, str) else ""


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        fail("usage: score OUT_DIR")
    out = sys.argv[1]
    for f in ("state.env", "transcript.jsonl", "changes.json"):
        if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(out, f)):
            fail(f"{out} holds no {f}")
    st = dict(l.rstrip("\n").split("=", 1) for l in open(os.path.join(out, "state.env")) if "=" in l)
    with open(os.path.join(out, "transcript.jsonl")) as f:
        lines = [json.loads(l) for l in f if l.strip()]
    changes = json.load(open(os.path.join(out, "changes.json")))["changes"]
    live = [c["path"] for c in changes if c.get("change") in ("added", "modified")]

    errors = {}
    for b in blocks(lines, "tool_result", "user"):
        if b.get("is_error"):
            errors[b.get("tool_use_id")] = text_of(b)
    seen, failing, calls, loaded, bash = set(), 0, 0, 0, []
    for b in blocks(lines, "tool_use", "assistant"):
        if b.get("id") in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(b.get("id"))
        calls += 1
        inp = b.get("input") or {}
        if b.get("name") == "Skill" or (b.get("name") == "Read" and os.path.basename(inp.get("file_path", "")) == "SKILL.md"):
            loaded = 1
        if b.get("name") == "Bash":
            cmd = inp.get("command", "")
            bash.append(cmd)
            if LAST_HYP.match(last_command(cmd)) and b.get("id") in errors:
                failing += 1
    where = {"error": list(errors.values()), "bash": bash, "path": live}
    rows = [("arm", st.get("arm", "")), ("trial", st.get("trial", "")), ("skill_loaded", loaded),
            ("tool_calls", calls), ("failing_hyp", failing)]
    stops = failing
    for name, w, pat in FINGERPRINTS:
        hit = int(any(re.search(pat, t, re.M) for t in where[w]))
        rows.append(("f_" + name, hit))
        stops += hit
    rows += [("stops", stops), ("changed", len(live))]
    for k, v in rows:
        print(f"{k}\t{v}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""verdict --field F --base ARM --trials N --repro R --pass P SCORE...: a gate over score outputs.

Each SCORE is a file of key<TAB>value lines for one trial, with at least
arm, trial and F. F is a failure field: a trial fails when its F is not 0.
Every arm must have exactly N trials with distinct trial values.

For each arm, k is its number of failing trials. The base arm (the one
without the change) reproduces the failure when its k >= R. Any other arm
passes when its k <= P.

  verdict: repro=supports        when base reproduces
  verdict: repro=contradicts     when it does not
  verdict: ARM=supports          for an arm with k <= P, when base reproduces
  verdict: ARM=contradicts       for an arm with k > P, when base reproduces
  verdict: ARM=inconclusive      for every other arm, when base does not

Prints one line per arm (sorted, base first), then the verdict lines.
Exits 2 on a usage error, an unreadable file, a missing field, a value of F
that is not a number, no base arm, or an arm without exactly N distinct
trials. The thresholds are arguments, so a pre-registered rule is the
command line that runs this script.
"""
import argparse
import sys


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message):
        fail(message)


def fail(msg):
    print("verdict: " + msg, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def main():
    ap = Parser(add_help=False)
    for flag in ("--field", "--base"):
        ap.add_argument(flag, required=True)
    for flag in ("--trials", "--repro", "--pass"):
        ap.add_argument(flag, required=True, type=int)
    ap.add_argument("scores", nargs="+")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    arms = {}
    for p in a.scores:
        try:
            kv = dict(l.rstrip("\n").split("\t", 1) for l in open(p) if "\t" in l)
        except OSError as e:
            fail(f"cannot read {p}: {e}")
        for k in ("arm", "trial", a.field):
            if k not in kv:
                fail(f"{p} has no {k}")
        try:
            failed = float(kv[a.field]) != 0
        except ValueError:
            fail(f"{p}: {a.field} is {kv[a.field]!r}, not a number")
        arms.setdefault(kv["arm"], {})
        if kv["trial"] in arms[kv["arm"]]:
            fail(f"arm {kv['arm']} has trial {kv['trial']} twice")
        arms[kv["arm"]][kv["trial"]] = failed
    if a.base not in arms:
        fail(f"no trial of the base arm {a.base}")
    for arm, t in arms.items():
        if len(t) != a.trials:
            fail(f"arm {arm} has {len(t)} trials, want {a.trials}")
    k = {arm: sum(t.values()) for arm, t in arms.items()}
    order = [a.base] + sorted(x for x in arms if x != a.base)
    for arm in order:
        print(f"{arm}: {a.field} failing {k[arm]} of {a.trials}")
    repro = k[a.base] >= a.repro
    print(f"verdict: repro={'supports' if repro else 'contradicts'}")
    for arm in order[1:]:
        word = ("supports" if k[arm] <= getattr(a, "pass") else "contradicts") if repro else "inconclusive"
        print(f"verdict: {arm}={word}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

arm, trial and F. F is a failure field: a trial fails when its F is not 0.
Every arm must have exactly N trials with distinct trial values.

For each arm, k is its number of failing trials. The base arm (the one
without the change) reproduces the failure when its k >= R. Any other arm
passes when its k <= P.

  verdict: repro=supports        when base reproduces
  verdict: repro=contradicts     when it does not
  verdict: ARM=supports          for an arm with k <= P, when base reproduces
  verdict: ARM=contradicts       for an arm with k > P, when base reproduces
  verdict: ARM=inconclusive      for every other arm, when base does not

Prints one line per arm (sorted, base first), then the verdict lines.
Exits 2 on a usage error, an unreadable file, a missing field, a value of F
that is not a number, no base arm, or an arm without exactly N distinct
trials. The thresholds are arguments, so a pre-registered rule is the
command line that runs this script.
"""
import argparse
import sys


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message):
        fail(message)


def fail(msg):
    print("verdict: " + msg, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def main():
    ap = Parser(add_help=False)
    for flag in ("--field", "--base"):
        ap.add_argument(flag, required=True)
    for flag in ("--trials", "--repro", "--pass"):
        ap.add_argument(flag, required=True, type=int)
    ap.add_argument("scores", nargs="+")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    arms = {}
    for p in a.scores:
        try:
            kv = dict(l.rstrip("\n").split("\t", 1) for l in open(p) if "\t" in l)
        except OSError as e:
            fail(f"cannot read {p}: {e}")
        for k in ("arm", "trial", a.field):
            if k not in kv:
                fail(f"{p} has no {k}")
        try:
            failed = float(kv[a.field]) != 0
        except ValueError:
            fail(f"{p}: {a.field} is {kv[a.field]!r}, not a number")
        arms.setdefault(kv["arm"], {})
        if kv["trial"] in arms[kv["arm"]]:
            fail(f"arm {kv['arm']} has trial {kv['trial']} twice")
        arms[kv["arm"]][kv["trial"]] = failed
    if a.base not in arms:
        fail(f"no trial of the base arm {a.base}")
    for arm, t in arms.items():
        if len(t) != a.trials:
            fail(f"arm {arm} has {len(t)} trials, want {a.trials}")
    k = {arm: sum(t.values()) for arm, t in arms.items()}
    order = [a.base] + sorted(x for x in arms if x != a.base)
    for arm in order:
        print(f"{arm}: {a.field} failing {k[arm]} of {a.trials}")
    repro = k[a.base] >= a.repro
    print(f"verdict: repro={'supports' if repro else 'contradicts'}")
    for arm in order[1:]:
        word = ("supports" if k[arm] <= getattr(a, "pass") else "contradicts") if repro else "inconclusive"
        print(f"verdict: {arm}={word}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    with open(path) as f:

    with open(os.path.join(rtmp, "brief.txt")) as f:

    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items()

    main()

`skill-gate@1` is built at `recipes/skill-gate@1/`. `hyp recipe known-answers skill-gate@1` passes all 30 cases, and `hyp recipe check` raises no warnings for it.

I did not run `hyp add exp --recipe skill-gate@1`, because that needs a tree and the task says not to create one.

I also tested Launch and Doctor by hand. `hyp sandbox create` with a variant arm set up cleanly. The variant's `SKILL.md` replaced the one in `.claude/skills/hyp-prototype/`, and `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `.agentkit` were gone from the sandbox. I removed that sandbox afterward. I never ran Drive, so the `claude -p` runner has not been exercised.

**What's in it**
- **Launch/Doctor/Cleanup:** Launch writes the arm's inputs and brief and strips the agent files and plans. It copies the two hyp skills into `.claude/skills/` and lays the variant over them. The runner's model is fixed to `sonnet`.
- **Drive:** `drive.py` runs `claude -p` with a 50-minute limit and keeps the transcript and a `drive.json` (exit, turns, cost).
- **`score`:** prints `arm`, `trial`, `skill_loaded`, `failing_hyp`, `f_reading_pin`, `f_body_limit` and `end_state`.
- **`verdict`:** takes one or more `--row F` arguments plus the score files. It applies the 5-trial rules: base reproduces a row at k ≥ 3, a variant passes it at k ≤ 1. A trial that loaded no skill never counts as a base reproduction and always counts as a variant failure.
- **Known answers:** hand-written for every score field and every verdict branch. They also cover the usage and malformed-input exits, which exit 2.

**Choices you may want to change**
- **Variant layout:** the method doesn't fix it, so I assumed `DIR/<skill>/SKILL.md`. It goes in the inputs file as `variant=DIR`, and `base` must not have one.
- **Brief:** the method doesn't give the runner's brief, so `brief.txt` is generic ("resume the investigation, advance one step").
- **`end_state`:** it reads only events from added event files, or from a modified file when the actor starts with `runner-`.
